gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a plug-in home-backup system costs per kWh. The cheapest whole-home-capable kits cost $431–$529 per kWh at the maker's store today (Growatt HELIOS 3600 at $431, Bluetti Apex 300 + 2× B300K at $445, or $529 with Bluetti's $699 Home Integration Kit added). EnergySage puts the Tesla Powerwall 3 at $998/kWh and the FranklinWH aPower 2 at $1,177/kWh. So, before the electrician's labor, a plug-in kit buys about twice the stored energy per dollar.
standout_why: I checked EnergySage's whole-home backup page (cited), Solar.com's best-batteries page (cited) and Solar Examiner's best-backup page (cited). All three give $/kWh, but only for installed wall batteries: Powerwall 3, aPower 2, Enphase 5P/10C, Renon, EG4 and EcoFlow Ocean Pro. None of them includes EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X, Anker SOLIX, Bluetti or Growatt, which ChatGPT shows as a card. None works out a cost per kWh for those units or compares them with installed batteries. Solar Examiner and Solar.com give no runtime per product. ChatGPT's answers list a single $7,899 DPU X price but never turn it into $/kWh.
decides: The Powerwall 3 stays the pick for permanent, solar-integrated whole-home backup ($998/kWh installed, 11.5 kW). For a shopper without solar who wants essential-circuit or partial-home backup, the derived figure makes Bluetti Apex 300 + 2× B300K ($445/kWh; $529/kWh with its home panel kit) the value pick on our page, ahead of DPU X ($643/kWh, or $797/kWh with the Smart Transfer Kit). The Anker S5000 ($517/kWh, 51.8 Wh/lb) is the pick if it has to roll. The caveat stays on the page: plug-in prices are hardware only, without the electrician, and their continuous output is 3.6–4.5 kW, against 11.5 kW for the Powerwall 3.

Tesla Powerwall 3 price on tesla.com: the product page lists no price. I used EnergySage's and Solar.com's installed figures instead.

Round-trip or inverter efficiency for the plug-in units, which I needed to turn nominal kWh into runtime at a stated load: I did not find it on the maker pages I opened, so I left out hours-at-1-kW figures.
